item.description: Mouria coffeehouse unable to renew lease in Exarchia, known for leftwing solidarity, resistance and radicalism It has been the hangout of writers, artists, poets and politicians, doctors and lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries for as long as anyone can remember. And for 44 years, Christos Vanas, the proprietor of Mouria, has let them all in. Every day at 7am, the taciturn former waiter has been the first man to step inside the historic cafe in Exarchia, the heart of leftwing Athens . Police said the woman, who lives in Sau Mau Ping, told the force at about 5am on Saturday that she had received the call earlier this month from a suspected scammer. He claimed her bank account, the one she used to buy insurance online, had been involved in money laundering and allegedly instructed her to transfer... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Judge Blocks Farm Amphitheater: court backs conservation easement; landowner may appeal
item.description: A recent ruling by a Superior Court judge has put the brakes on the proposed outdoor amphitheater at Union Grove Farm, North Carolina. The Triangle Land Conservancy raised alarms over land-use regulations intended to safeguard agricultural landscapes. This dispute stems from a conservation easement put in place during the 1990s, underscoring the ongoing conflict between developmental ambitions and environmental protection in the area. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: US organ donation group faces decertification after Kentucky man’s near-fatal ordeal
item.description: TJ Hoover II's case raised critical alarms when he showed signs of life just before organ retrieval, prompting intense scrutiny of patient safety protocols. item.description: This story was first published on October 31, 1971.
